q: R and S are different digits from 1 through 9. What digit does S represent?
key: Answer: B. RSS = 100R + 11S, and RS = 10R + S, so RSS − RS = 90R + 10S = 260. Testing valid digits: R=2 gives S=8 (both valid, 1-9, distinct) -- this is the only combination that works. Check: 288 − 28 = 260, and every column subtracts cleanly with NO borrowing needed (8−2=6 in the tens place).

q: The floor of Room A is in the shape of a square and has an area of 121 feet². The floor of Room B is in the shape of a rectangle and has a length of 7 feet and width of 15 feet. Which statement correctly compares the floors in the two rooms?

choices.A: The area of the floor in Room A is the same as the area of the floor in Room B.
choices.C: The area of the floor in Room A is less than the area of the floor in Room B.
choices.D: The perimeter of the floor in Room A is less than the perimeter of the floor in Room B.
choices.B: The perimeter of the floor in Room A is equal to the perimeter of the floor in Room B.

key: Answer: B. Room A is a square with area 121 ft², so its side length is 11 ft and its perimeter is 4 × 11 = 44 ft. Room B's area is 7 × 15 = 105 ft² (not equal to 121, so the two area-comparison choices are both false). Room B's perimeter is 2(7+15) = 44 ft -- the SAME as Room A's perimeter, even though the areas are different. You have to compute both area AND perimeter for both rooms before you can tell which comparison is true.

q: A parking lot is 35 full. Of the cars in the parking lot, 20% of them are blue. If the parking lot has 100 total parking spots, how many blue cars are in the parking lot?

q: 4,000 milliliters is equal to how many kiloliters?
key: Answer: D. 1 kiloliter = 1,000,000 milliliters (1 kL = 1,000 L, and 1 L = 1,000 mL). So 4,000 mL ÷ 1,000,000 = 0.004 kL. This is a two-step metric jump (mL → L → kL), which is exactly where a factor-of-10 slip creeps in.
ref: Tier: Medium · Topic: Multi-step unit conversion (off-by-10, multi-step) · Diagram: no · Real, unused library item (global_id 203) -- CONFIRMED WRONG, and confirmed off by exactly a factor of 10 (she circled 0.04 instead of 0.004) -- a direct, real hit on this exact named gap.

q: If the volume of a rectangular prism is 72 in³, which equation can be used to determine the height of the prism if the length is 6? (V = lwh, where V = volume, l = length, w = width, and h = height.)
key: Answer: B. V = lwh, so 72 = 6 × w × h, which means w × h = 12. Solving for h: h = 12/w.

topic: Classification of Numbers, given a Set
q: Two numbers are greater than 1. One is a prime number and the other is an odd number. What will always describe the product of the two numbers?
key: Answer: C. A prime number has exactly two factors (1 and itself). Multiplying it by another number greater than 1 always creates a number with MORE than two factors -- which makes it composite, no matter which prime or odd number you pick. Example: prime 2 × odd 5 = 10 (composite). Example: prime 5 × odd 7 = 35 (odd AND composite) -- the only thing true in both examples is "composite."

q: Justin had some coins in a bag. He counted 38 coins that were silver and 27 coins that were copper. What fraction of the coins that Justin had were silver?
key: Answer: A. The part is the silver coins (38); the whole is ALL the coins (38 + 27 = 65). Fraction silver = 3865. (Using 27 as the denominator or numerator instead of the 65 total gives a part-to-part ratio instead of part-to-whole.)

q: Use the pattern to help answer the question: 1+3=2², 1+3+5=3², 1+3+5+7=4². What is the solution to 1+3+5+7+9+11+13+15?
key: Answer: C. Each time you add one more odd number, the base number on the right goes up by 1. Continuing: 1+3+5+7+9=5², +11=6², +13=7², +15=8². So the full sum 1+3+5+7+9+11+13+15 = 8².

q: Two cubes are shown. Cube A has sides of length 2 units and Cube B has sides of length 4 units. How many Cube A's can fit inside of Cube B?
key: Answer: B. Volume of Cube A = 2×2×2 = 8 cubic units. Volume of Cube B = 4×4×4 = 64 cubic units. 64 ÷ 8 = 8 Cube A's fit inside Cube B. (Doubling the side length multiplies the VOLUME by 2³=8, not by 2 -- a very common trap, which is why 4 is also offered as a choice.)

topic: No Remainder when Divided by a given Number
q: Which whole number is divisible by 6 without a remainder?
key: Answer: C. A number is divisible by 6 if it's divisible by BOTH 2 and 3. 732 is even (divisible by 2), and its digit sum 7+3+2=12 is divisible by 3 -- so 732 is divisible by 6 (732 ÷ 6 = 122). None of the other choices pass both checks.

topic: Finding Area/Perimeter of Rectangle, given Length & Width
q: The width of a rectangle is Y meters. Which statement correctly compares the value of Y to the length of the rectangle, where Y = 14 × length?

choices.A: The value of Y is always 14 times the value of the length.
choices.D: The value of Y is always 34 times the value of the length.
choices.B: The value of Y is always 3 times the value of the length.
choices.C: The value of Y is always 4 times the value of the length.

key: Answer: A. The equation directly states Y = 14 × length -- so Y is always 14 of the length. (B swaps in the COMPLEMENT, 34, instead of the fraction actually given in the equation -- a complement-confusion trap, the same kind of mix-up as the 'decreased by 30%' language gap.)

q: Brandon used a number machine. Each number he put in came out as a different number, according to one consistent rule. Some examples are shown in the table. Which statement describes the relationship between the number Brandon put into the machine and the number that came out of it?

choices.B: The output was 2 more than the input.
choices.A: The output was 2 less than the input.
choices.D: The output was 5 more than the input.
choices.C: The output was 5 less than the input.

key: Answer: B. Check each pair: 10→12, 15→17, 24→26, 41→43 -- every output is exactly 2 more than its input.

q: Which expression is equal to (2 + 8) × 7?
key: Answer: D. By the distributive property, a(b+c) = ab + ac, so (2+8)×7 = 2×7 + 8×7. (Check directly: (2+8)×7 = 10×7 = 70, and only this expression also equals 70.)
ref: Tier: Medium · Topic: Order of Operations and Equivalence · Diagram: no · Real, unused library item (ISEE Lower #3 Q29), used verbatim, answered correctly -- a distributive-property-equivalence item, different shape than QR8 #8's plain simplify-both-groups version.

topic: Remainder when Divided by a given Number
q: Which expression results in a remainder of 5?
key: Answer: C. 35 ÷ 6 = 5 remainder 5 (6×5=30, 35−30=5). Check the others: 32÷6=5 r2, 33÷6=5 r3, 34÷6=5 r4 -- only D leaves remainder 5.

q: The 2nd number in a pattern is 19, the 3rd number is 31, and the 4th number is 43. What is the 1st number in the pattern?
key: Answer: B. The common difference is 12 (31−19=12, 43−31=12). Working backward: 1st number = 19 − 12 = 7. (12 is the DIFFERENCE, not the 1st term -- the same off-by-one-direction trap as QR7 #35. 55 extends the pattern FORWARD instead of backward, which isn't what's asked.)

topic: Remaining Amount after Reducing by Fractions
q: Lois had 4 pencils and 6 pens. She lost 12 of her pencils and 13 of her pens. How many pencils and pens does she have remaining, combined?
key: Answer: C. Pencils remaining: lost 12 of 4 = 2, so 4 − 2 = 2 left. Pens remaining: lost 13 of 6 = 2, so 6 − 2 = 4 left. Combined: 2 + 4 = 6.
ref: Tier: Medium · Topic: Remaining Amount after Reducing by Fractions · Diagram: no · Real, unused library item (ISEE Lower #1 Q25) -- CONFIRMED WRONG on the real test (she picked B, 5) -- two different fractions applied to two different starting amounts in one problem, more demanding than a single-fraction version.

q: Which phrase is represented by the expression (46 − 22) ÷ 2?

choices.D: 22 less than the quotient of 46 and 2
choices.C: 46 more than the quotient of 22 and 2

key: Answer: A. (46 − 22) is "the difference of 46 and 22." Dividing that difference by 2 is the same as taking HALF of it -- so "half the difference of 46 and 22."
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Translating Math Expressions · Diagram: no · Real, unused library item (global_id 106, ISEE Lower #2), used verbatim, answered correctly -- the reverse direction (expression → phrase) from the usual phrase → expression format, for variety.

q: Alika is buying 23 shirts that cost $18.99 each. Which expression can be used to find the best estimate of how much it will cost Alika to buy the shirts?
key: Answer: B. Round each number to the nearest ten: 23 rounds to 20, and $18.99 rounds to $20. Since this is a total COST for many items, you multiply (not add): 20 × 20.

q: Manny has a total of 228 eggs. Using these eggs, he will fill empty egg cartons that each hold 12 eggs. What is the greatest number of egg cartons that Manny can fill completely?
key: Answer: C. 228 ÷ 12 = 19 full cartons exactly.

q: Use the number line shown. The hash marks are evenly spaced. What is the mean (average) of A and B?
key: Answer: A. There are 9 equal intervals between 10 and 37, a total span of 27, so each interval = 27 ÷ 9 = 3. A is 2 intervals from 10 (A = 10 + 2×3 = 16); B is 6 intervals from 10 (B = 10 + 6×3 = 28). Mean of A and B = (16 + 28) ÷ 2 = 22.
